site_descricao: Polpad One: an open source 18-key macropad with a display, built around the ESP32-C3. Download the Polpad software, the firmware and the 3D case, and browse community projects.
comunidade_intro: Cases, profiles, builds and firmware made by Polpad users. Every project is reviewed before it is published.
comunidade_intro2: This is where projects made from the Polpad One live. There are cases, with variations of the box, keycaps and stands; profiles, with ready-made settings for the software, OBS, Photoshop or games; builds, from people who put theirs together and show the parts and what changed; and firmware, modified by those who wanted to go further. Each project comes with photos, a description, the files to download and the license that says how it can be reused.
comunidade_intro3: To take part, you send your project through GitHub, straight from the browser, with nothing to install. Once it is reviewed, it joins this page for others to download, build and improve. The button below leads to the step-by-step guide.

projeto_intro: Polpad One is the first board, not the last. The next step is freeing the software from a fixed layout: when you plug in a board, it will work out on its own how many keys it has, the screen size and even whether it has a screen. That way, any macropad can be set up with the same software, without starting from scratch.
projeto_intro2: And the next board could be yours. Designed a new case, put together a profile, made an improvement or a whole macropad? Send the files and a few photos, and tell us how you got there. After a review, your project joins the community, so others can build it, adapt it and take the idea further.
sobre_a: Keyboard shortcuts make a computer faster, but most people only use a few. Many shortcuts are barely known, others take three or more keys at once, and sometimes a program simply has no shortcut for what you need. A macropad improves on that: each key becomes a shortcut, a whole key combination or a sequence of actions, all with a single press. Commercial models, however, are closed and expensive: you cannot see the software, repair it or adapt it. Polpad started from a question: can you build a cheap, configurable macropad with visual feedback that anyone can reproduce, repair and improve?
sobre_b: The premise is open hardware and open software. The board, the case, the firmware and the software are published under free licenses (GPL-3.0 and CERN-OHL-S), and the Polpad One costs about R$ 122 in parts. The project began as an academic paper and continues here, with the downloads and the community.
